## Check of the proposed answer

The answer $n/t$ cannot be correct, because it contradicts the ordering of the ensemble.

**Ordering bound.** The KPZ line ensemble is ordered, $\mathcal{H}^{(t)}_{n+1}(x)\le \mathcal{H}^{(t)}_n(x)$ for all $n$, $x$, and $t$. So $\mathcal{H}^{(t)}_{n+1}(x)-\mathcal{H}^{(t)}_n(x)\le 0$, which gives
$$
0 < \mathbb{E}\big[e^{\mathcal{H}^{(t)}_{n+1}(x)-\mathcal{H}^{(t)}_n(x)}\big] \le 1 \quad\text{for all } n,\ t,\ x.
$$

**Counterexample.** Take $n=1$ and $t<1$. The proposed value is $1/t>1$, which violates the bound. Take $n=2$ and $t=1$. The proposed value is $2>1$, which also violates it. So $n/t$ is false for general $n$ and $t$.

**Where the derivation fails.** The integration-by-parts relations are consistent. Gaussian integration by parts gives $\mathbb{E}[\partial_\omega U(s,\mathcal{H}_n(s))] = g_n''(s)$, with the sign checked against a linear-potential example. The $n=1$ step $A_1 = 1/t$ is also consistent with the top-layer Galilean symmetry.

The error is the step asserting $g_k''(x) = -1/t$ for every layer $k$. The top-layer shear argument does not transfer to higher layers in this normalization. If the curvatures were all equal to a common constant $-\kappa$, the recursion would force $A_n = A_1 + (n-1)\kappa$, which grows without bound and again violates $A_n \le 1$. So the recursion itself, with the proposed curvatures, is incompatible with the ordering. I have not identified the exact correct value of the expectation.

The final answer $n/t$ is not correct.

VERDICT: REJECT
